audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Hoshea, Assyrian siege and deportation, theological retrospective, imperial resettlement, lion narrative, and mixed-worship communities, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for vassal tribute, imprisonment, three-year siege, mass deportation, retrospective blame, child-through-fire, prophetic warning, Judah's inclusion, Assyrian population transfer, settler vulnerability, lions, imported priest, local and ancestral worship, and later Samaritan reception.

verses.restored: In twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king in Samaria over Israel and reigned nine years.

familiar.text: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years.

modern.text: In the twelfth year of the reign of Ahaz over Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria nine years.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לְאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ הוֹשֵׁ֨עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֧ה בְשֹׁמְר֛וֹן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תֵּ֥שַׁע שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: He did evil in eyes of YHWH, only not as kings of Israel who were before him.

familiar.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, but not like the kings of Israel who preceded him.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה רַ֗ק לֹ֚א כְּמַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו

verses.restored: Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him; Hoshea became his servant and returned tribute to him.

familiar.text: Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents.

modern.text: Shalmaneser king of Assyria attacked him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute.

original.text: עָלָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה שַׁלְמַנְאֶ֖סֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַֽיְהִי ל֤וֹ הוֹשֵׁ֨עַ֙ עֶ֔בֶד וַיָּ֥שֶׁב ל֖וֹ מִנְחָֽה

verses.restored: King of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and did not bring tribute to king of Assyria year by year. King of Assyria confined him and bound him in prison.

familiar.text: And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year: therefore the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison.

modern.text: But the king of Assyria discovered that Hoshea had conspired to send envoys to King So of Egypt, and that he had not paid tribute to the king of Assyria as in previous years. Therefore the king of Assyria arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Israel Carried Captive to Assyria

original.text: וַיִּמְצָא֩ מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֨וּר בְּהוֹשֵׁ֜עַ קֶ֗שֶׁר אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙ אֶל ס֣וֹא מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וְלֹא הֶעֱלָ֥ה מִנְחָ֛ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר כְּשָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֑ה וַֽיַּעַצְרֵ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֖הוּ בֵּ֥ית כֶּֽלֶא

verses.restored: King of Assyria went up through all land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.

familiar.text: Then the king of Assyria came up throughout all the land, and went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.

modern.text: Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land, marched up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶ֖יהָ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: In ninth year of Hoshea, king of Assyria captured Samaria, exiled Israel to Assyria, and settled them in Halah and Habor by river Gozan and in cities of Medes.

familiar.text: In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

modern.text: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and carried away the Israelites to Assyria, where he settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְהוֹשֵׁ֗עַ לָכַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ אֶת שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיֶּ֥גֶל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַשּׁ֑וּרָה וַיֹּ֨שֶׁב אֹתָ֜ם בַּחְלַ֧ח וּבְחָב֛וֹר נְהַ֥ר גּוֹזָ֖ן וְעָרֵ֥י מָדָֽי

verses.restored: This happened because children of Israel sinned against YHWH their Divine, who brought them up from land of Egypt from under hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they revered other gods.

familiar.text: For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,

modern.text: All this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. They had worshiped other gods

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּֽי חָטְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם הַמַּעֲלֶ֤ה אֹתָם֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִתַּ֕חַת יַ֖ד פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים

verses.restored: They walked in statutes of nations whom YHWH dispossessed from before children of Israel, and in statutes kings of Israel had made.

familiar.text: And walked in the statutes of the heathen, whom the LORD cast out from before the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which they had made.

modern.text: and walked in the customs of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites, as well as in the practices introduced by the kings of Israel.

original.text: וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ בְּחֻקּ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ

verses.restored: Children of Israel covered over things that were not right against YHWH their Divine and built high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the LORD their God, and they built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.

modern.text: The Israelites secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. From watchtower to fortified city, they built high places in all their cities.

original.text: וַיְחַפְּא֣וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל דְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא כֵ֔ן עַל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּבְנ֨וּ לָהֶ֤ם בָּמוֹת֙ בְּכָל עָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם מִמִּגְדַּ֥ל נוֹצְרִ֖ים עַד עִ֥יר מִבְצָֽר

verses.restored: They set up pillars and Asherim for themselves on every high hill and under every green tree.

familiar.text: And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree:

modern.text: They set up for themselves sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

original.text: וַיַּצִּ֧בוּ לָהֶ֛ם מַצֵּב֖וֹת וַאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים עַ֚ל כָּל גִּבְעָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה וְתַ֖חַת כָּל עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן

verses.restored: There they burned incense at all high places, like nations YHWH exiled from before them, and did evil things to provoke YHWH.

familiar.text: And there they burnt incense in all the high places, as did the heathen whom the LORD carried away before them; and wrought wicked things to provoke the LORD to anger:

modern.text: They burned incense on all the high places like the nations that the LORD had driven out before them. They did wicked things, provoking the LORD to anger.

original.text: וַיְקַטְּרוּ שָׁם֙ בְּכָל בָּמ֔וֹת כַּגּוֹיִ֕ם אֲשֶׁר הֶגְלָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ דְּבָרִ֣ים רָעִ֔ים לְהַכְעִ֖יס אֶת יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: They served idols, concerning which YHWH had said to them, You shall not do this thing.

familiar.text: For they served idols, whereof the LORD had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing.

modern.text: They served idols, although the LORD had told them, “You shall not do this thing.”

original.text: וַיַּֽעַבְד֖וּ הַגִּלֻּלִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: YHWH warned Israel and Judah through every prophet and every seer, saying, Turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments and statutes according to all Torah I commanded your fathers and sent to you through my servants the prophets.

familiar.text: Yet the LORD testified against Israel, and against Judah, by all the prophets, and by all the seers, saying, Turn ye from your evil ways, and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the prophets.

modern.text: Yet through all His prophets and seers, the LORD warned Israel and Judah, saying, “Turn from your wicked ways and keep My commandments and statutes, according to the entire Law that I commanded your fathers and delivered to you through My servants the prophets.”

original.text: וַיָּ֣עַד יְהוָ֡ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וּבִיהוּדָ֡ה בְּיַד֩ כָּל נביאו כָל חֹזֶ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר שֻׁ֝֠בוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֤ם הָֽרָעִים֙ וְשִׁמְרוּ֙ מִצְוֺתַ֣י חֻקּוֹתַ֔י כְּכָ֨ל הַתּוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶת אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדַ֥י הַנְּבִיאִֽים

verses.restored: But they did not listen and hardened their neck like neck of their fathers, who did not trust in YHWH their Divine.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding they would not hear, but hardened their necks, like to the neck of their fathers, that did not believe in the LORD their God.

modern.text: But they would not listen, and they stiffened their necks like their fathers, who did not believe the LORD their God.

original.text: וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּקְשׁ֤וּ אֶת עָרְפָּם֙ כְּעֹ֣רֶף אֲבוֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א הֶאֱמִ֔ינוּ בַּֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: They rejected his statutes, covenant he cut with their fathers, and testimonies by which he warned them. They went after emptiness and became empty, and after nations around them, concerning whom YHWH commanded them not to do like them.

familiar.text: And they rejected his statutes, and his covenant that he made with their fathers, and his testimonies which he testified against them; and they followed vanity, and became vain, and went after the heathen that were round about them, concerning whom the LORD had charged them, that they should not do like them.

modern.text: They rejected His statutes and the covenant He had made with their fathers, as well as the decrees He had given them. They pursued worthless idols and themselves became worthless, going after the surrounding nations that the LORD had commanded them not to imitate.

original.text: וַיִּמְאֲס֣וּ אֶת חֻקָּ֗יו וְאֶת בְּרִיתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֣ת אֶת אֲבוֹתָ֔ם וְאֵת֙ עֵֽדְוֺתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵעִ֖יד בָּ֑ם וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ אַחֲרֵ֤י הַהֶ֨בֶל֙ וַיֶּהְבָּ֔לוּ וְאַחֲרֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר סְבִֽיבֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֖י עֲשׂ֥וֹת כָּהֶֽם

verses.restored: They abandoned all commandments of YHWH their Divine, made two cast calves, made an Asherah, bowed to all host of heavens, and served Baal.

familiar.text: And they left all the commandments of the LORD their God, and made them molten images, even two calves, and made a grove, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.

modern.text: They abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God and made for themselves two cast idols of calves and an Asherah pole. They bowed down to all the host of heaven and served Baal.

original.text: וַיַּעַזְב֗וּ אֶת כָּל מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם מַסֵּכָ֖ה שנים עֲגָלִ֑ים וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֲשֵׁירָ֗ה וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֙ לְכָל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֶת הַבָּֽעַל

verses.restored: They made their sons and daughters pass through fire, practiced divination and omens, and sold themselves to do evil in eyes of YHWH, provoking him.

familiar.text: And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, and used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke him to anger.

modern.text: They sacrificed their sons and daughters in the fire and practiced divination and soothsaying. They devoted themselves to doing evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

original.text: וַֽ֠יַּעֲבִירוּ אֶת בְּנֵיהֶ֤ם וְאֶת בְּנֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּקְסְמ֥וּ קְסָמִ֖ים וַיְנַחֵ֑שׁוּ וַיִּֽתְמַכְּר֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ

verses.restored: YHWH became very angry with Israel and removed them from before his face; none remained except tribe of Judah alone.

familiar.text: Therefore the LORD was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.

modern.text: So the LORD was very angry with Israel, and He removed them from His presence. Only the tribe of Judah remained,

original.text: וַיִּתְאַנַּ֨ף יְהוָ֤ה מְאֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְסִרֵ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו לֹ֣א נִשְׁאַ֔ר רַ֛ק שֵׁ֥בֶט יְהוּדָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Judah also did not keep commandments of YHWH their Divine but walked in statutes Israel had made.

familiar.text: Also Judah kept not the commandments of the LORD their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they made.

modern.text: and even Judah did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God, but lived according to the customs Israel had introduced.

original.text: גַּם יְהוּדָ֕ה לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ר אֶת מִצְוֺ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ בְּחֻקּ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ

verses.restored: YHWH rejected all seed of Israel, afflicted them, and gave them into hand of plunderers until he cast them from before his face.

familiar.text: And the LORD rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his sight.

modern.text: So the LORD rejected all the descendants of Israel. He afflicted them and delivered them into the hands of plunderers, until He had banished them from His presence.

original.text: וַיִּמְאַ֨ס יְהוָ֜ה בְּכָל זֶ֤רַע יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיְעַנֵּ֔ם וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיַד שֹׁסִ֑ים עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁלִיכָ֖ם מִפָּנָֽיו

verses.restored: For he tore Israel from house of David; they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king, and Jeroboam drove Israel from following YHWH and caused them to sin a great sin.

familiar.text: For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the LORD, and made them sin a great sin.

modern.text: When the LORD had torn Israel away from the house of David, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king, and Jeroboam led Israel away from following the LORD and caused them to commit a great sin.

original.text: כִּֽי קָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵעַל֙ בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֔ד וַיַּמְלִ֖יכוּ אֶת יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן נְבָ֑ט וידא יָרָבְעָ֤ם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְהֶחֱטֵיאָ֖ם חֲטָאָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה

verses.restored: Children of Israel walked in all sins Jeroboam did; they did not turn from them,

familiar.text: For the children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did; they departed not from them;

modern.text: The Israelites persisted in all the sins that Jeroboam had committed and did not turn away from them.

original.text: וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּכָל חַטֹּ֥אות יָרָבְעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה לֹא סָ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנָּה

verses.restored: until YHWH removed Israel from before his face, as he spoke through all his servants the prophets. Israel was exiled from its land to Assyria to this day.

familiar.text: Until the LORD removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.

modern.text: Finally, the LORD removed Israel from His presence, as He had declared through all His servants the prophets. So Israel was exiled from their homeland into Assyria, where they are to this day. Samaria Resettled

original.text: עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁר הֵסִ֨יר יְהוָ֤ה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד כָּל עֲבָדָ֣יו הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים וַיִּ֨גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל מֵעַ֤ל אַדְמָתוֹ֙ אַשּׁ֔וּרָה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: King of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in cities of Samaria in place of children of Israel. They possessed Samaria and lived in its cities.

familiar.text: And the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel: and they possessed Samaria, and dwelt in the cities thereof.

modern.text: Then the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the towns of Samaria to replace the Israelites. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns.

familiar.text: Wherefore they spake to the king of Assyria, saying, The nations which thou hast removed, and placed in the cities of Samaria, know not the manner of the God of the land: therefore he hath sent lions among them, and, behold, they slay them, because they know not the manner of the God of the land.

modern.text: So they spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, “The peoples that you have removed and placed in the cities of Samaria do not know the requirements of the God of the land. Because of this, He has sent lions among them, which are indeed killing them off.”

translation_notes: Samaria's fall follows a three-year imperial siege and mass deportation. The theological retrospective must not erase Assyrian violence, civilian suffering, starvation, imprisonment, and forced population transfer.
Exile is not proof that displaced people deserved displacement. Communities under conquest must not be blamed for the violence an empire inflicted upon them.

The chapter critiques Israel and Judah through covenant theology, but its polemic against surrounding nations cannot authorize racism, xenophobia, colonial dispossession, or contempt for minority religions.
Children made to pass through fire are victims of adult religious and political systems. Child sacrifice is abuse and must never become a sensational marker of supposedly inferior peoples.

Assyria deliberately moves populations from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim into depopulated Samaritan cities. These settlers are also displaced subjects of empire, not voluntary invaders in a modern sense.
The lion account reflects ancient land-theology and danger in disrupted ecosystems. Animal attacks must not be preached as evidence that migrants practice the wrong religion.
The imported priest teaches a state-managed version of local religion. Imperial religious policy can control populations while appearing to accommodate them.

The resulting communities combine traditions. Mixed religious identity is described critically by the narrator but must not be used to persecute interfaith families, plural communities, or Samaritans.
Later anti-Samaritan prejudice and Christian supersessionism are categorically rejected. Samaritans are a living ethnoreligious community, not a synonym for corruption or half-faith.
The phrase 'to this day' belongs to the narrator's horizon and requires compositional audit.
safety_note: Do not blame exiles for deportation, stigmatize migrants or religiously mixed communities, preach animal attacks as punishment, or weaponize this chapter against Samaritans, Jews, interfaith families, or minority religions. Keep Assyrian colonial violence, child victims, displaced settlers, and the narrator's polemical perspective visible at the same time.
